docs.title: ChirpQuiz
docs.text: ChirpQuiz is a free, ad-free app for learning to identify more than 8,000 bird species by their calls. I developed it to combine listening quizzes with tools for targeted practice.

docs.title: Quiz and learning features
docs.text:
• Five quiz types: explore birds by area, observation frequency, scientific classification, personal lists, or learning status.
  • Two ways to play: use Training to practice at your own pace, or Challenge to test your knowledge with three lives and a score.
  • Expert mode and adjustable difficulty: select an answer from all birds in the current quiz, or use four choices with configurable answer similarity and other difficulty settings.
  • Learning progress: Training is optimized for learning. Each bird's learning status is available in the My Lists tab.
  • Bird information and maps: consult species information and distribution data on a map. Distribution data and the OpenStreetMap map are included in the app and available offline.

See the user guide for details about quiz types, quiz modes, difficulty, and learning progress.

docs.title: Explore
docs.text:
• User guide: instructions and feature details.
  • Privacy policy: information about data handling.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text:
I'm Julien Levarlet, the developer of ChirpQuiz. For questions or suggestions, email me or visit the Discord community.

The app uses bird data from GBIF, recordings from Xeno-canto, and information and images from Wikipedia and Wikimedia.

docs.title: How Birds Are Selected
docs.text:
There are two different selections in each question:

  1. The target bird is the species whose recording you hear.
  2. The other three answer choices are distractors. Their similarity is controlled by the difficulty setting.

Difficulty does not usually change the target pool. The quiz type and, for area-based quizzes, your selected area and season determine which target birds are eligible.

With Expert mode enabled, you choose the target from a searchable list of all birds eligible for the current quiz instead of choosing from four answer buttons.

docs.title: Quiz types
docs.text:
Quiz Birds that can appear General Quiz Birds in the selected area and season, narrowed by the observation-frequency range. The range is part of difficulty settings. If it leaves too few species, the quiz falls back to all birds matching the area and season. Common Birds The most frequently observed birds in the selected area and season. Choose a level for the 10, 20, or 30 most common species. My Lists Birds in the list you selected. Create and manage lists in Search. A list needs at least four birds to be used in a quiz. Learning Mode Birds in the learning-status group you selected: Review, Learning, or Mastered. Groups with too few birds are not offered as quiz levels. Classification Birds in a selected scientific group, such as an order, family, or genus, within your area and season. Available groups depend on those settings.

Area and season filters are used for General, Common Birds, and Classification quizzes. My Lists uses the contents of your list, Learning Mode uses your saved learning status.

docs.title: How distractors are chosen
docs.text:
The app uses bird classification to find alternatives at the similarity level you selected. For example, closer choices may come from the same family or genus. It tries to use birds from the current quiz's eligible pool, so a question stays consistent with that quiz. If the pool does not contain enough choices at the requested similarity, the app broadens the search to less closely related groups.

With Expert mode off, a multiple-choice question needs four eligible birds. If there are too few, try a broader area, another season or quiz, or a list with more birds.

docs.title: Learning and repetition
docs.text:
The app uses a Leitner spaced-repetition system in Training: birds you are still learning come back sooner, while birds you identify consistently are shown less often. For more details, see the Leitner system on Wikipedia.

Challenge uses a simple random order and does not use that spaced-repetition queue. Your learning status is still updated from your answers and is visible in My Lists, you can also choose a status as a quiz level in Learning Mode.

docs.title: Difficulty
docs.text: Choose a preset in the quiz options, or select Custom to adjust the three controls independently. Difficulty settings are saved on your device.

docs.title: Presets
docs.text:
Presets combine answer similarity, the maximum number of recordings considered for a species, and an observation-frequency range for the General Quiz.

Preset General Quiz observation range What to expect Beginner 0-25% Most frequently observed species and easier-to-distinguish answer choices. Easy 5-40% Common species, with somewhat closer choices. Intermediate 10-50% A broader mix and more closely related alternatives. Hard 20-75% A broad range of species and challenging alternatives. Expert 25-100% Includes less frequently observed species and the closest alternatives available.

The percentages describe a relative range of species ranked by observations in your selected area, not a promise of an exact number of birds. The range only filters the General Quiz. Common Birds has its own 10/20/30 selection, while other quiz types use their own bird pools.

docs.title: Answer similarity
docs.text: Move from Beginner toward Expert to make the incorrect answers more closely related to the target species. The app uses classification groups to find those alternatives. This changes the answer choices, not which target bird is selected.

docs.title: Recording variety
docs.text: Choose how many Xeno-canto recordings may be considered for a species, from 1 to 20. The app selects a recording from that set, so a higher value can provide more variety when recordings are available. It does not guarantee that every species has that many recordings.

docs.title: Observation frequency
docs.text: Set the lower and upper bounds of the relative observation range. Lower percentages focus on more frequently observed species, higher percentages include less frequently observed species. A wider range makes more species eligible. This setting affects only the General Quiz.

docs.title: Expert mode
docs.text: Expert mode is a separate switch that changes how you answer: instead of four choices, you search and select the bird from all species eligible for the current quiz. It does not change the quiz's bird pool or replace the difficulty controls. In Challenge, each correct answer is worth one point.

docs.title: What changes in Expert mode?
docs.text: Instead of four answer buttons, Expert mode lets you search and choose from all the birds eligible for the current quiz. It changes how you answer, not which birds are included. In Challenge, a correct answer is worth one point. See Quiz modes.

docs.title: Why do I hear the same bird again?
docs.text: Training uses the Leitner spaced-repetition system: birds you are still learning return sooner, while birds you identify consistently appear less often. Repeats are normal, especially in a small quiz. See Learning and scoring.

docs.title: Where can I see my learning progress?
docs.text: The Achievements tabs is there to check your progress, there you can see all of your scores, with a global progression score based on birds learning status. Open the My Lists tab in the search to see each bird's learning status. Your answers update that status in both Training and Challenge.

docs.title: Can I use ChirpQuiz offline?
docs.text: No, you cannot play quizzes offline at the moment. However, you can still browse the app, see your scores and search for birds offline. While you are offline, no images, sounds or wikipedia abstract will be available.

docs.title: Why is a recording missing or not playing?
docs.text: Quiz recordings come from Xeno-canto and need an internet connection. Check your connection and media volume, then try again.

docs.title: Where can I report a problem or send a suggestion?
docs.text: I'm still developing ChirpQuiz, so your feedback is welcome. Email me or find my contact information under Settings > Contact in the app.

docs.title: Choose a quiz
docs.text:
Open the Quiz tab and choose Training or Challenge. Expand a quiz to read its description, then select it to see its available level and options. The information icon on a quiz explains what it is for.

If prompted, choose an area in Settings. An area helps ChirpQuiz show species relevant to you. You can also choose a season, All includes species across seasons.

docs.title: Answer a question
docs.text:
1. Listen to the bird recording. Tap the bird image to pause or resume playback.
  2. Choose the species from the four answer buttons, or—if Expert mode is on—search for it in the list of birds available in that quiz.
  3. In Training, a wrong answer does not end the question. Try again, the image may reveal more as you make mistakes, depending on your image setting.
  4. When the answer is revealed, continue to the next question. You can choose automatic or manual advancement in Settings.

In Training, press and hold an answer after the question is answered to see a short Wikipedia summary when one is available.

docs.title: If a question will not load
docs.text:
Quiz recordings are fetched from Xeno-canto, so check your internet connection and media volume. If playback reports an error, use the reload option shown in the quiz.

For ways to explore bird details outside a quiz, see Settings and the other tabs and Bird data, recordings, and images.

docs.title: Learning and Scoring
docs.text: ChirpQuiz tracks your learning progress. You can see each species' general learning status in the My Lists tab. The status describes how consistently you have identified the bird.

docs.title: How a bird's learning status changes
docs.text:
Each bird has a learning score from 0 to 3. A bird with no saved history starts at 0.

Score Status in the app Meaning 0 Review New or needs more practice. 1 or 2 Learning Some progress has been recorded, but the bird is not yet consistently identified. 3 Mastered The bird has reached the top of the learning scale.

When a question is completed, a correct answer on the first attempt raises the bird's score by one, up to 3. If you make one or more mistakes before eventually answering correctly in Training, that completed question lowers the score by one instead. In Challenge, a wrong answer ends the question and lowers the score by one.

This is a small progression scale, not a percentage or a measured certainty. The app also records correct and incorrect outcomes, but the three statuses above are based on the 0-to-3 score. You can find birds by learning status in My Lists, or choose a status as a level in Learning Mode when there are enough birds in it.

docs.title: How Training decides what to ask next
docs.text: The app uses a Leitner spaced-repetition system in Training: birds you are still learning come back sooner, while birds you identify consistently are shown less often. The review queue is separate for each quiz and level. For more about the method, see the Leitner system on Wikipedia. Challenge uses a random order, while still updating your general learning status when a question is resolved.

docs.title: How Challenge points work
docs.text:
Training does not award Challenge points. In Challenge, a correct answer adds points and a wrong answer costs one of the three lives. The number of points per correct answer depends on the challenge type:

  • Finite Challenge quizzes award 1 point per correct answer.
  • Endless General Quiz Challenge normally calculates points from how closely related the three incorrect choices are to the target bird.
  • With Expert mode enabled, every correct answer is worth 1 point, including in the endless General Quiz.

For the endless General Quiz scoring calculation, the app compares the target species with its three distractors:

Relationship to the target Base points At least one distractor is in the same genus 6, plus 1 for each additional same-genus distractor No same-genus distractor, but at least one is in the same family 3 No same-family match, but at least one is in the same order 2 No match at those levels 1

There is an additional point when at least two distractors share the target's family but are from a different genus. The final value is capped at 9. In general, close taxonomic alternatives make the question worth more because they are harder to distinguish.

The score displayed during Challenge is the current run's total. The trophy value is your saved best for that quiz level and area/season selection. The app saves a new best when the run exceeds the previous score, and records whether a finite challenge has been completed.

docs.title: Expert mode is not the same as Expert difficulty
docs.text:
These are separate settings:

  • Expert difficulty makes distractors more closely related to the target bird in multiple-choice quizzes. In the General Quiz it also selects a less common observation-frequency range and considers more recordings.
  • Expert mode replaces the four answer buttons with a searchable list of all birds in the current quiz. In Challenge, each correct answer is worth one point, the mode does not change the quiz pool or number of lives.

See Difficulty for the difficulty presets and custom controls, and Quiz Modes for how Training and Challenge differ.

docs.title: Bird data, recordings, and images
docs.text: I bring together bird information from a few independent sources: GBIF for bird data and distribution information, Xeno-canto for recordings, and Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons for summaries and images. These projects provide the content, I don't own or create it.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
• GBIF: bird data, including distribution information.
  • Xeno-canto: bird recordings. You can contribute recordings on Xeno-canto.
  • Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons: bird summaries and images. You can contribute to Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons.

docs.title: Support ChirpQuiz
docs.text:
I'm still developing ChirpQuiz, and feedback from people using it helps me improve it. Please contact me with bug reports, suggestions, questions, or ideas about the bird selection and learning experience.

Email me: birdquiz.contact@gmail.com

You can also find contact information in Settings > Contact in the app. A review on the app store can help other bird learners discover ChirpQuiz, too.

docs.title: Quiz Modes
docs.text: The mode switch on the Quiz screen changes the experience for all quiz types.

docs.title: Training
docs.text:
Training is for learning at your own pace. A wrong answer does not cost a life, and you can keep practicing. Most Training quizzes are endless: the app keeps presenting birds using the quiz's selection rules and learning system. The score is not the focus.

In Training, you can press and hold an answer after a question is answered to read a Wikipedia summary when available.

docs.title: Challenge
docs.text:
Challenge is a scored game with three lives. A wrong answer costs a life, the challenge ends when you run out. Correct answers add points. Scoring depends on the quiz: finite quizzes award one point for each correct answer, while the endless General Quiz normally awards more points when its answer choices are taxonomically close. See Learning and scoring for the full rules.

Challenge quizzes have a saved best score and completion status. Some challenges use a finite set of birds, while the General Quiz challenge continues until you lose. The quiz descriptions and How birds are selected explain the contents of each type.

docs.title: Expert mode
docs.text: Expert mode is a separate switch in the quiz options, alongside the difficulty selector. Instead of four answer buttons, it gives you a list to search and choose from, containing all the birds eligible for the current quiz. It changes how you answer, not which birds the quiz includes, use the difficulty setting to change how similar the usual multiple-choice alternatives are. In Challenge, Expert mode makes each correct answer worth one point as there is no distractors to confuse you.

docs.title: Answering in either mode
docs.text:
In Training, you can retry after a wrong answer. In Challenge, the first answer decides whether the question is correct, so choose carefully. With Expert mode on, select your answer from the searchable bird list instead of the four choices. Once a question is answered, the next question starts automatically or waits for you, according to Next question in Settings.

The top of the quiz shows your current score and best score. Remaining lives are shown in Challenge.

docs.title: Learning progress
docs.text: Answers also update your learning progress, regardless of whether you play Training or Challenge. You can see each species' learning status in My Lists. Training uses a Leitner spaced-repetition system to decide which birds to show next. These are related but separate systems, Learning and scoring explains them.

docs.title: Area and season
docs.text:
Choose an area on the map in Settings to focus area-based quizzes on local birds. Choose a season to limit the selection to species present in that season, or choose All. If you want to remove the area filter, use the location reset option.

Changing the area or season can change the birds and levels available in quizzes. Some classification groups may disappear when they do not have enough eligible species.

docs.title: Images in quizzes
docs.text:
Choose when to show bird images:

  • Always shows the image from the start in Training.
  • Gradually reveals more after mistakes.
  • Never keeps the quiz focused on listening.

docs.title: Playback and questions
docs.text:
• Next question can advance automatically or wait for you to continue.
  • Audio normalization adjusts playback loudness to make recordings easier to compare.
  • Use your device's media volume if a recording is too quiet.

docs.title: Languages
docs.text: The app language controls menus and messages. The bird language controls bird names and the language used when looking up bird information. If a translated bird name is not available, the app may use the English bird page instead.

docs.title: Search and bird details
docs.text:
Use Search to look up birds by common or scientific name. In Area follows your current area and season, All Birds searches the full bird database, and My Lists lets you create quiz lists and check each bird's learning status. A bird's detail page can show a Wikipedia summary and image, Xeno-canto recordings, and links to other reference resources when available and online.

Bird distribution information and the OpenStreetMap map are included in the app and are available offline. Recordings, Wikipedia summaries, and some other reference information are loaded online.

The app's information and credits area links to the source projects and provides developer contact and review options.

docs.title: Privacy Policy
docs.text: This privacy policy applies to the ChirpQuiz mobile application (the "Application") created by Julien Levarlet (the "Service Provider") as a free service. This service is provided "AS IS".

docs.title: Privacy at a glance
docs.text:
• 100% local storage: All scores, achievements, and game progress stay on your device.
  • No account required: You can play without creating an account or logging in.
  • No tracking or profiling: We do not collect personal data, track your location, or build user profiles.
  • No personal server data: We do not operate servers that store your personal information.

docs.title: Data collection and local storage
docs.text:
ChirpQuiz is designed to respect your privacy. The Application does not collect or store personally identifiable information on external servers.

All game-related data, such as scores, unlocked achievements, and quiz progress, is stored locally on your device only. The Application does not track your precise location, collect user analytics, or display targeted advertisements.

docs.title: Third-party content services
docs.text:
To display bird images and audio recordings, the Application connects directly to public APIs. When your device fetches this content, it makes a standard HTTP request directly to those servers.

As with any internet connection, these third-party servers automatically receive standard technical metadata needed to fulfill the request:

  • App identifier (User-Agent): An HTTP header identifying "ChirpQuiz" so third-party APIs can monitor traffic according to their fair-use policies.
  • Your IP address: Transmitted automatically by your network to receive the requested image or sound.

No user account, user profile, or game data is ever sent. For details on how these services log and handle technical network data, such as IP addresses, refer to their respective policies:

  • Wikimedia Privacy Policy
  • Xeno-canto Terms & Privacy

docs.title: External links
docs.text: The Application may contain links to external websites, such as Wikipedia, Xeno-canto, GBIF, and the IUCN Red List. If you click a third-party link, you will be redirected to that site. These external sites are not operated by the Service Provider. We advise you to review their privacy policies.

docs.title: Data retention and deletion
docs.text: Since all game progress and settings are stored locally on your device, uninstalling the Application automatically and permanently deletes all app data. No data remains on external servers because none was sent.

docs.title: Children's privacy
docs.text: The Application does not knowingly solicit or collect personally identifiable information from children under 13. Since no personal data is collected from any user, children's privacy is protected by design. Parents or guardians with concerns can contact us at birdquiz.contact@gmail.com.

docs.title: Legacy users (Google Play Games data)
docs.text:
If you used a previous version of ChirpQuiz integrated with Google Play Games, historical scores and achievements may still be stored on Google's servers. The current version no longer connects to Google Play Games, so this data is no longer accessed or used.

To permanently delete past Play Games data for ChirpQuiz through your Android device:

  1. Open the Google Play Games app.
  2. Tap the three-dot menu or profile avatar and open Settings.
  3. Select Delete Play Games account & data.
  4. Under Delete individual game data, find ChirpQuiz and tap Delete.

docs.title: Changes to this policy
docs.text:
This Privacy Policy may be updated from time to time. Changes will be reflected on this page. You are advised to review it periodically.

This privacy policy is effective as of September 8, 2026.

docs.title: Contact us
docs.text:
For questions regarding privacy while using the Application, contact the Service Provider at birdquiz.contact@gmail.com.

Politique de confidentialité en français

docs.title: ChirpQuiz User Guide
docs.text:
ChirpQuiz helps you learn bird sounds through short listening quizzes. Choose a quiz, listen to a recording, and identify the species. You can practice without score pressure or take on a challenge with three lives.

This guide explains how the quizzes choose birds and answers, what the difficulty settings change, and where the app's bird information and recordings come from.

docs.title: Help improve ChirpQuiz
docs.text:
I'm still developing ChirpQuiz, and your feedback can help me make it better. Please contact me to report bugs, point out confusing parts, request features, or share ideas about the quizzes and bird information.

Email me: birdquiz.contact@gmail.com

You can also open Settings > Contact in the app to find the contact information. The app may also invite you to send feedback after you have learned a few birds.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Getting started: choose a quiz and answer your first question.
  • Quiz modes: understand Training and Challenge.
  • How birds are selected: see what each quiz includes and how answer choices are built.
  • Difficulty: tune answer similarity, recording variety, and observation frequency.
  • Learning and scoring: understand learning-status changes, Training repetition, Challenge points, and Expert mode.
  • Settings: adjust area, season, images, languages, and playback.
  • Bird data, recordings, and images: see where the app's bird information, recordings, and images come from.
  • FAQ: quick answers to common questions.

docs.title: A quick note about quiz settings
docs.text:
The selected area and season affect which birds are available in area-based quizzes. The difficulty setting mainly affects how similar the three incorrect answers are to the correct bird. These are separate controls, see How birds are selected and Difficulty for details.

Parts of this guide were drafted with AI assistance and checked against the app's current behavior. Details may change as ChirpQuiz develops.

docs.title: CuiQuiz
docs.text: CuiQuiz est une application gratuite et sans publicité pour apprendre à identifier plus de 8 000 espèces d'oiseaux grâce à leurs chants. Je l'ai développée pour associer des quiz d'écoute à des outils d'entraînement adaptés.

docs.title: Fonctionnalités
docs.text:
• Cinq types de quiz : découvrir les oiseaux par zone, fréquence d'observation, classification scientifique, listes personnalisées ou statut d'apprentissage.
  • Deux modes de jeu : s'entraîner à son rythme ou relever un défi avec trois vies et un score.
  • Mode expert et difficulté réglable : choisir parmi toutes les espèces du quiz en mode expert, ou répondre parmi quatre choix avec différents niveaux de difficulté.
  • Suivi de l'apprentissage : l'entraînement utilise optimise l'apprentissage. Le statut d'apprentissage de chaque oiseau est consultable dans l'onglet My Lists.
  • Fiches d'espèces et cartes : consulter les informations et les données de répartition des oiseaux sur une carte.

Le guide d'utilisation, disponible en anglais, présente les types de quiz, les modes de jeu, la difficulté et le suivi de l'apprentissage.

docs.title: Explorer
docs.text:
• Guide d'utilisation : présentation des fonctionnalités et instructions (en anglais).
  • Politique de confidentialité : informations sur le traitement des données.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text:
Je suis Julien Levarlet, le développeur de CuiQuiz. Pour toute question ou suggestion, écrivez-moi ou consultez le Discord.

L'application utilise des données ornithologiques de GBIF, des enregistrements de Xeno-canto et des informations et images de Wikipedia et Wikimedia.

docs.title: Politique de confidentialité
docs.text: Cette politique de confidentialité s'applique à l'application mobile CuiQuiz (l'« Application ») créée par Julien Levarlet (le « Fournisseur de services ») à titre de service gratuit. Ce service est fourni « TEL QUEL ».

docs.title: La confidentialité en un coup d'œil
docs.text:
• Stockage 100 % local : Tous vos scores, succès et votre progression restent exclusivement enregistrés sur votre appareil.
  • Aucun compte requis : Vous n'avez besoin d'aucun compte ni d'aucune connexion pour jouer.
  • Aucun suivi ni profilage : Aucune donnée personnelle n'est collectée, aucune géolocalisation ni aucun profil d'utilisateur.
  • Aucune donnée personnelle sur serveur : Nous n'hébergeons aucun serveur stockant des informations vous concernant.

docs.title: Collecte de données et stockage local
docs.text:
CuiQuiz est conçue dans le respect de votre vie privée. L'Application ne collecte et ne transmet aucune information personnelle identifiable vers des serveurs distants.

Toutes les données liées au jeu, telles que vos scores, votre progression et vos paramètres, sont conservées uniquement en local sur votre appareil. L'Application ne collecte pas votre position GPS précise, ne réalise aucun suivi publicitaire et n'affiche aucune publicité ciblée.

docs.title: Services tiers de contenu
docs.text:
Pour afficher les photos d'oiseaux et les enregistrements sonores, l'Application se connecte directement à des API publiques. Lorsque votre appareil télécharge ces éléments, il envoie une requête HTTP standard à leurs serveurs.

Comme pour tout échange sur Internet, ces serveurs tiers reçoivent automatiquement les métadonnées techniques nécessaires au transfert :

  • Identifiant de l'application (User-Agent) : Un en-tête HTTP identifiant « ChirpQuiz », requis par les API pour respecter leurs conditions d'utilisation.
  • Votre adresse IP : Transmise automatiquement par votre réseau pour recevoir l'image ou le son.

Aucun compte utilisateur, profil ou donnée de jeu n'est transmis. Pour en savoir plus sur la façon dont ces services gèrent les journaux réseau et les adresses IP, consultez leurs politiques respectives :

  • Politique de confidentialité de Wikimedia
  • Conditions et confidentialité de Xeno-canto

docs.title: Liens externes
docs.text: L'Application peut contenir des liens vers des sites web externes, par exemple Wikipédia, Xeno-canto, GBIF et la Liste rouge de l'UICN. Si vous cliquez sur un lien tiers, vous serez redirigé vers ce site. Ces sites ne sont pas exploités par le Fournisseur de services, nous vous invitons à consulter leur politique de confidentialité.

docs.title: Conservation et suppression des données
docs.text: Puisque l'ensemble de vos données de jeu est stocké localement sur votre appareil, la désinstallation de l'Application supprime automatiquement et définitivement toutes vos données. Aucune donnée ne subsiste sur un serveur distant puisqu'aucune n'y a été envoyée.

docs.title: Protection des enfants
docs.text: L'Application ne sollicite ni ne collecte sciemment de données personnelles auprès d'enfants de moins de 13 ans. Aucune donnée personnelle n'étant collectée auprès des utilisateurs, la vie privée des enfants est protégée par conception. Pour toute question, les parents ou tuteurs peuvent écrire à birdquiz.contact@gmail.com.

docs.title: Anciens utilisateurs (données Google Play Jeux)
docs.text:
Si vous avez utilisé une version précédente de ChirpQuiz connectée à Google Play Jeux, vos anciens scores et succès peuvent toujours être conservés sur les serveurs de Google. La version actuelle de l'application n'étant plus liée à ce service, ces données ne sont plus consultées ni utilisées.

Pour supprimer définitivement vos anciennes données de jeu Google depuis votre appareil Android :

  1. Ouvrez l'application Google Play Jeux.
  2. Ouvrez les Paramètres depuis le menu ou l'avatar de profil.
  3. Sélectionnez Supprimer le compte Play Jeux et les données.
  4. Sous Supprimer des données d'un jeu, recherchez CuiQuiz et appuyez sur Supprimer.

docs.title: Modifications de cette politique
docs.text:
Cette politique peut être mise à jour occasionnellement. Toute modification sera publiée sur cette page. Il est conseillé de la consulter régulièrement.

Cette politique est effective à compter du 8 septembre 2026.

docs.title: Nous contacter
docs.text:
Pour toute question concernant la confidentialité lors de l'utilisation de l'Application, contactez le Fournisseur de services à birdquiz.contact@gmail.com.

English privacy policy
